# everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials (Ephemeral Resource)

Requests temporary credentials for the platform console of a Storage Pool: a `username` and an expirable `password`. Log in with them, create your own users, and use those from then on. The Storage Pool must have the platform console enabled.

-> **This is meant for the initial setup of the platform console.** Use it only when you need credentials: remove the block once the setup is done, keep it in a separate configuration, or use `count` to skip it in other runs.

Every `terraform plan` and `terraform apply` that evaluates this resource requests new credentials and invalidates the previous password, including plan-only and refresh runs. The password is valid until `expires_at`. Users you created yourself are never affected.

Requires Terraform 1.10 or later, and 1.11 or later to pass the password to a write-only attribute.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Store the credentials in an Azure Key Vault secret.
#
# Run this configuration only when you need platform console credentials. Every
# plan and apply issues new credentials and invalidates the previous password, so keep it apart
# from the configuration that manages your infrastructure.
#
# Requires Terraform 1.11 or later, for write-only attributes.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
    azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = ">= 4.23.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

provider "azurerm" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
  features {}
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

data "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  name                = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
}

data "azurerm_key_vault" "example" {
  name                = "kv-storage-prod"
  resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
}

ephemeral "everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials" "this" {
  storage_pool_id = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
}

# value_wo_version changes on every run, so the secret always holds the password this run
# issued and not an earlier one that has already been invalidated.
resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "console_activation_credentials" {
  name             = "storage-pool-console-activation-credentials"
  key_vault_id     = data.azurerm_key_vault.example.id
  value_wo         = ephemeral.everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials.this.password
  value_wo_version = parseint(formatdate("YYYYMMDDhhmmss", plantimestamp()), 10)
}
```

```terraform
# Hand the credentials to a script.
#
# Run this configuration only when you need a platform console credentials. Every
# plan and apply issues a new code and invalidates the previous one, so keep it apart
# from the configuration that manages your infrastructure.
#
# Requires Terraform 1.10 or later.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

data "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  name                = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
}

ephemeral "everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials" "this" {
  storage_pool_id = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
}

# The provisioner runs at apply only, never during plan. triggers_replace runs it on
# every apply, each time with the code that apply just issued. The code goes in
# environment, not in command: command-line arguments are visible to other users of
# the machine. Terraform hides the script's output while the code is in its
# environment. If the script fails, the apply fails and shows the script's output in
# full, so the script must never print the code.
resource "terraform_data" "console_setup" {
  triggers_replace = plantimestamp()

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "./setup-console-user.sh"
    environment = {
      CONSOLE_USERNAME = ephemeral.everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials.this.username
      CONSOLE_PASSWORD = ephemeral.everpure_azure_platform_console_activation_credentials.this.password
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `storage_pool_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the Storage Pool. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When the password expires, in UTC, formatted as RFC 3339 (for example `2026-10-02T14:30:00Z`).
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Expirable password for `username`, valid until `expires_at`.
- `username` (String) Name of the console user to log in as with the password.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `open` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when requesting the activation credentials.
